definition.text: Catalysis of the reaction: adenosine + H2O = inosine + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: adenosine + H2O = inosine + NH4+, in a tRNA molecule.
Catalysis of the reaction: adenosine + H2O = inosine + NH4+, in a double-stranded RNA molecule.
Catalysis of the reaction: adenosine-37 + H2O = inosine-37 + NH4+, in a tRNA-Ala molecule.
Catalysis of the reaction: an adenosine-phosphate + H20 = an inosine phosphate + NH4+. Catalyzes the deamination of AMP, ADP or ATP.
Catalysis of the reaction: adenosine34 in tRNA + H2O + H+ = inosine34 in tRNA + NH4+.

A protein complex that possesses tRNA-specific adenosine-34 deaminase activity. In eukaryotes the complex is a heterodimer; the subunits are known as Tad2p and Tad3p in yeasts and Adat2 and Adat3 in human.
Catalysis of the reaction: 3',5'-cyclic AMP + H2O + H+ = 3',5'-cyclic IMP + NH4+.
The directed movement of adenosine, adenine riboside, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
Binding to an enzyme that catalyzes the removal of an amino group from a substrate, producing ammonia (NH3).
Catalysis of the removal of an amino group from a substrate, producing a substituted or nonsubstituted ammonia (NH4+/NH2R).
Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + H2O + H+ = ITP + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + adenosine = ADP + AMP.

The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of adenosine, adenine riboside, a ribonucleoside found widely distributed in cells of every type as the free nucleoside and in combination in nucleic acids and various nucleoside coenzymes.
